annotationRationale: The common ratio expresses both neighboring terms, while its reduced form and the prime-power structure of 720 restrict its numerator and denominator and prove minimality.
sourceMethod: Follows the official reduced-rational-ratio method, the construction with ratio 16/15, and the contradiction using only three distinct primes. The denominator bounds and exceptional cases 16 and 17 are made explicit.

review.mathCheck: Reduced numerator m and denominator n must be coprime divisors of 720. A ratio strictly between 1 and 16/15 requires n>15; n=16 forces the invalid m=17, and n=17 is impossible. Larger m,n each need two distinct prime factors, contradicting coprimality within {2,3,5}. Thus b=768 and its digit sum is 21, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 12 across pages 6–7. It retains the reduced-ratio and disjoint-prime-factor argument while explicitly supplying the small-denominator exclusions behind the official minimality proof.
review.annotationCheck: Geometric-sequence ratios and prime-exponent restrictions are appropriately assessed. Reduced fractions supply the coprimality background. No material concept omission.
